hook: A silver alarm clock with a crowd of hands, each one counting down to the end of something. The fun of this file is in the list: every hand gets its own short entry, and the inscriptions swing from cosmic to trivial without warning. Read it like a catalog of small jokes and small dreads, and take your time with the notes under each hand.
whyItMatters: Tagged as both a collaboration and a rewrite, it uses a list format that lets many small ideas sit side by side, including gags aimed at the Foundation's own bureaucracy and even at the site that hosts it. It shows how one simple rule, a hand reaching twelve, can hold up a whole mosaic of micro-stories. In passing it also nods to other entries such as SCP-094 and SCP-343.
thingsToNotice: The notes do the real work: most inscriptions are a single line, and the researcher commentary underneath turns them into jokes, puzzles or warnings. The hand concerned with the clock's own classification is a neat self-referential gag about how object classes get decided. Elsewhere, the entry about a Class-D subject shows in a few sentences what it means for the clock to be unbeatable. Notice too how much is blacked out, and which hands the file chooses not to explain at all.

related.note: Cited in one hand's note as a point of comparison.
